title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — imputation of Adam's death? unheard-of; then 'sinned in Adam' can stand without sin imputed
pass_a_gloss: Placeus balks at 'imputation of Adam's death' as unheard-of. His parallel stands: if dying in Adam can be true without Adam's death imputed, sinning in Adam can be true without Adam's sin imputed.
pass_b_english: PLAC. Really—to the imputation of Adam's death? Who ever heard that Adam's death is imputed to us? So my answer—or if you will, my argument—stands: if the proposition "we die in Adam" is true even though Adam's death is not imputed to us, the proposition "we sinned in Adam" can also be true even though Adam's sin is not imputed to us.
source_text: PLAC. Itane, ad imputationem mortis Adami? Quis unquam audiverat, mortem Adami nobis imputari? Manet igitur responsio mea, vel si ita vis, argumentatio: si propositio in Adamo morimur vera est, quamvis mors Adami nobis non imputetur, etiam propositio in Adamo peccavimus vera esse potest, quamvis peccatum Adami nobis non imputetur.

choices.choice: Adam death imputed unheard; parallel for sin without imputation
